1.mascotDialogue: Same values, beta, but TWO views — a tree for the ordering rule, an array for how it actually lives in memory. parent(i) equals (i minus 1) divided by 2 — that's it, the whole address book, right there.

2.mascotDialogue: Line 3 is the array-to-tree bridge, beta: any index's parent is always (i-1)/2, integer division, no rounding tricks. Line 4 is the min-heap rule itself — stop the moment the parent is already smaller or equal.

3.mascotDialogue: Hover index 4 in the array, beta — watch its tree node light up as a child of index 1! Same data, two synchronized windows looking at the exact same thing.

4.mascotDialogue: Both the array cell and the tree node light up in the same broken color at once, beta — because it is ONE violation, just being viewed two different ways at the same time.
